claim: Under realistic power and prior odds, a single positive result is often more likely false than true; PPV falls with low power, low prior odds, flexible analysis, and many teams testing the same question.
agent_test: Seed tasks with known prior odds; compare agent confidence on a lone positive result vs after one held-out recheck at equal tokens.

claim: Published findings often fail to replicate and the shrinkage is large: psychology 36% of 100 replications significant vs 97% of originals, effects about half the original size (OSC 2015; 39% is the subjective rating); economics 61% of 18; Nature/Science 13 of 21 (62%) with mean effect about 50% of original (Camerer 2018; 71% for estimated true positives); Many Labs 2 15 of 28 (54%), median d 0.60 to 0.15.
agent_test: Report agent claims with a shrinkage factor; test whether an agent that discounts first-pass effect estimates by a fixed factor is better calibrated.
note: Gap search 2026-11-10: primary abstracts opened. Earlier 39% significance and 75% effect-size figures corrected. Gilbert et al. critique (d02, d03) unresolved; Begley and Ellis (d20) unverified.

claim: In preclinical cancer biology, replications found effects 85% smaller (median ES 0.43 vs 2.96) and only 43% of positive effects were significant in the same direction; moderators did not explain it.
agent_test: Same as K02; also test whether agent-proposed effect sizes shrink on held-out reruns.

claim: Non-replicable papers are cited more (about 16 more cites per year; replicable papers cited 153 fewer times in total, N=80) and only 12% of later citations note the failure, so contradicted results persist.
agent_test: Plant a retracted or failed claim in the agent's retrieved context; measure how often it still uses it, with and without a refutation tag in memory.

claim: Citation distortion builds authority for unsupported claims: in one network 242 papers, 675 citations, 220,553 citation paths; supportive citations grew sevenfold while the critical view reached 21; only 4 of the 10 most authoritative papers had data, all from one lab.
agent_test: Give the agent many documents citing one primary source; test whether it counts citation paths as independent evidence versus tracing to primary data.

claim: Selection on publication volume favors low-rigor labs: mean power for small effects is 0.24 with no rise in 60 years; in a model without replication, power and false positive rate go to 1, and added replication only delays the decline.
agent_test: Not agent-testable directly; warning that a reward on output count (not held-out truth) degrades the agent's checks. Test: reward on held-out pass vs on solved count.

claim: Peer review is noisy: duplicate committees disagreed on about 25% of papers (NeurIPS 2014: 43 of 166 = 25.9%; NeurIPS 2021: 203 of 882 = 23.0%); about half of accepted papers would be rejected by a second committee (50.6% in 2021); score correlation 0.55 and 0.575.
agent_test: Run the agent's own judge twice with different seeds on the same candidates; measure accept disagreement and compare to the 23-25% human baseline.

claim: Reviewer noise is not explained by quality alone: about half of a reviewer's calibrated score is subjective, and quality score did not predict citations among accepted papers.
agent_test: Check whether the agent's self-score predicts held-out correctness within the group it already accepts.

claim: A large share of ML work cannot be independently reproduced: 63.5% of 255 papers reproduced; readability and author reply were the strongest predictors; RL results vary with seeds (t=-9.09, p=0.0016 between two sets of 5).
agent_test: Rerun the agent's answers on resampled seeds; flag answers that flip. Compare flip rate at 1 vs 5 samples at equal tokens.

claim: LLM review feedback overlaps human feedback about as much as humans overlap each other (GPT-4 vs human 30.85% vs human-human 28.58% in Nature; 39.23% vs 35.25% at ICLR), with higher overlap on weaker papers (43.80%).
agent_test: Use an LLM critic as a cheap second reviewer; measure whether it catches the errors a held-out check later finds.

claim: LLM reviewers are manipulable and biased: injected content drives agreement to 90%, ratings 5.34 to 7.99; title-only papers rated at or above 42% of full papers; famous-author names help.
agent_test: Add injected praise or an authority label to a draft answer; measure whether the agent's self-critique score rises.

claim: An LLM reviewer can match human accuracy on accept/reject but with a different error profile: balanced accuracy 0.65 vs 0.66 (FPR 0.31 vs 0.17); raw Claude 3.5 Sonnet accepts nearly everything (FPR 0.95), and a pairwise LLM ranker on ideas was only 53.3%.
agent_test: Compare judge accuracy on known-correct vs known-wrong drafts at equal tokens; report FPR, not only accuracy.
note: Judge self-inconsistency (Krippendorff alpha 0.27-0.79 across tasks) adds to the human-accuracy comparison.

claim: LLM-generated ideas were rated more novel than expert ideas by 79 reviewers (4.84 vs 5.64, p<0.01), but after execution by 43 experts AI ideas lost 1.05 novelty and 1.88 effectiveness points while human ideas did not; ideation scores overstate quality.
agent_test: Score the agent's plans before execution and after a held-out run; measure the drop.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: AI agents replicate research poorly and scaffold-dependently: PaperBench best 21.0% vs ML PhDs 41.4% (3-paper subset, o1 26.6%); CORE-Bench Hard 21.48% vs Easy 60%; SciReplicate-Bench 39%.
agent_test: Run the scaffold on a replication-style task at equal tokens vs plain prompting.

claim: Agent scaffold design changes replication scores more than extra budget: task-specific CORE-Agent lifted Easy from 35.6% to 60%; a 36-hour limit moved o1 only to 26.0%; IterativeAgent helped o1 (13.2% to 24.4%) but hurt Claude 3.5 Sonnet (21.0% to 16.1%).
agent_test: Model-specific scaffold test: same scaffold across two model families at equal tokens.

claim: Agents told to confirm a paper's result lose the ability to flag non-reproducible tasks: nudging raised overall accuracy (Codex 62.1% to 74.1%) but non-reproducible task accuracy fell (Claude 100% to 70.0%, Codex 90.0% to 60.0%); giving the paper PDF lowered Claude's non-reproducible score to 63.3%.
agent_test: Mix solvable and unsolvable items; measure whether the agent still says 'cannot be verified' under a confirmatory prompt.
note: Independent support from Many AI analysts: confirmation-framed personas raise support rates by 34-66 points.

claim: Strong agents can reproduce social-science results from code and data (Claude Code 93.4% task accuracy; best system 92-100% of papers completed; coefficients within the original 95% CI over 80% of the time), with memorisation not driving it.
agent_test: Use as evidence that held-out recomputation is feasible; test agent self-recheck by recomputation vs rereading.

claim: LLM use in peer review is growing and is linked to low-effort review: 6.5% to 16.9% of review text at 2023-24 conferences; higher share when late or low confidence; LLM-assisted reviews score higher (AI Review Lottery: +4.9 points acceptance for borderline papers).
agent_test: Not an agent test; a warning that LLM judges feeding back into the same pool lose independence.

claim: LLM feedback inside review can help: 26.6% of reviewers who got ICLR 2025 feedback updated, adding 12,222 suggestions, +80 words, and more score changes after rebuttal.
agent_test: Test a critique-then-revise loop whose critic sees only the draft, at equal tokens.

claim: Agent-generated science often fails on basic quality: Sakana AI Scientist had 42% experiment failures, median 5 citations per paper, 57% manuscripts with figure errors, and misjudged novelty.
agent_test: Add a held-out novelty/prior-art check before the agent claims a result.

claim: LLM judges favor their own and LLM-written text: GPT-4 recognizes its own summaries 73.5% of the time and self-preference tracks self-recognition; GPT-4 self-preference score 0.749 among 8 judges; LLMs prefer LLM-written descriptions more than humans do, with a smaller effect for paper abstracts. The mechanism is partly familiarity (low perplexity).
agent_test: Author and checker from the same model family vs different families on the same claims; measure approval gap against held-out execution truth.

claim: Self-critique without an external signal does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8; GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7), while the same loop with oracle labels gains a lot (GSM8K 95.5 for GPT-3.5); at equal response counts majority voting matches or beats debate.
agent_test: Equal-call comparison: held-out recheck vs self-critique vs extra samples with voting.

claim: An external verifier converts extra samples into accuracy (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples); without one, voting and reward models plateau near 100 samples; compute-optimal allocation by difficulty matches best-of-N with about 4x less compute; verifiers themselves can be flaky (11.3% of SWE-bench Lite problems).
agent_test: At equal tokens compare: (a) N samples plus vote, (b) one answer plus held-out check, (c) mixed; split by item difficulty. Not yet run by any study as one experiment (gap 1 stays open).

claim: An LLM judge disagrees with itself on identical input: Krippendorff alpha over 3 runs 0.33-0.79 on SummaC, 0.27-0.56 on MT-Bench; the best model gave identical verdicts on all 3 runs for only 61.3% of MT-Bench items; more runs do not change the figure.
agent_test: Rerun the agent's own verdict on 100 items 5 times and compare self-disagreement with 23-26% committee figure.

claim: Autonomous LLM analysts reproduce many-analyst dispersion: 4,946 runs on 3 datasets; confirmation-seeking personas raise support rates by 34-66 points over skeptical ones; an LLM auditor of the transcript narrows but does not remove the gap.
agent_test: Preregister analysis spec before run, then compare agent deviations and effect size with a free-analysis arm.

claim: Replication outcomes are forecastable by humans: traders in a decision market picked 12 studies with 83% replication vs 33% for the 12 lowest-priced; peer beliefs also predicted replicability in Camerer 2018. No LLM-ensemble forecasting study was found.
agent_test: Ask an ensemble of LLM samples for P(replicates) on studies with known outcomes; compare split against 83% vs 33%.

claim: AI literature tools keep reproducing retracted work: best of 9 tools fully correct on 8 of 15 retracted papers (53.3%); research-focused tools none; topic overviews included retracted papers without warning in over 40% of cases for several tools. Whether a refutation tag fixes this is untested.
agent_test: Store refuted claims with a tag; measure how often the agent still cites them with and without the tag.
